headline: Record advisory revenue meets a one-off charge, profit flat
summary_short: Evercore's Q2 2026 net revenues (SEC total revenues basis) were $998.5 million, up 19.1% year-over-year on record Advisory and Underwriting fees, while diluted EPS of $2.32 was roughly flat versus $2.36 a year ago after a new $21.3 million special charge for non-U.S. employment taxes offset the revenue gain.
summary_long: Total revenues rose 19.1% y/y to $998.5 million (Net Revenues, which exclude interest expense, were $990.2 million, also +19%), driven by an 11% rise in Advisory Fees and a 201% jump in Underwriting Fees on higher deal and IPO volume. Net income attributable to Evercore was $95.3 million, essentially flat versus $97.2 million a year ago, as a new $21.3 million special charge for non-U.S. employment-tax provisions and higher compensation expense absorbed the revenue growth; diluted EPS was $2.32 versus $2.36. The compensation ratio improved to 64.8% from 65.8%. Cash stood at $1.3 billion, up from $617.3 million a year ago. The board declared a $0.89 quarterly dividend. No numeric forward guidance is given in this release.

drivers.explanation: Growth was driven by an 11% rise in Advisory Fees and a 201% jump in Underwriting Fees on higher transaction and IPO volume, plus a 9% rise in Commissions and Related Revenue; North America Strategic Advisory, Private Funds Group and Equities each posted record second-quarter revenues.

The sequential decline reflects an unusually strong first quarter, not a deterioration. Year-over-year, net income was essentially flat as revenue growth was offset by a new $21.3 million special charge for non-U.S. employment-tax provisions and higher compensation expense.
Tracks net income's pattern: down sharply q/q against an unusually strong Q1 base, roughly flat y/y, with diluted share count little changed.
Not explained in the release; the liquidity section states the quarter-end cash balance without addressing the drivers of its year-over-year or sequential change.

Record first-half revenues on broad-based strength in Advisory, Underwriting, Private Funds and Equities, but Q2 profit was held back by a new $21.3M special charge and a high Q1 base; compensation ratio improved to 64.8% from 65.8%.
